stem: A pharmacist directly oversees both sterile and complex nonsterile compounding. Which continuing-education statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Meet the applicable annual sterile-compounding CE requirement.
Use general pharmacy-law CE in place of all compounding CE.
Also assess the annual complex-nonsterile compounding CE requirement.
Apply compounding CE only to technicians.
Treat the applicable requirements as cumulative when both activities are supervised.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Meet the applicable annual sterile-compounding CE requirement. Also assess the annual complex-nonsterile compounding CE requirement. Treat the applicable requirements as cumulative when both activities are supervised.

choice_analysis.A: Supported: Meet the applicable annual sterile-compounding CE requirement.
choice_analysis.B: Not supported: Use general pharmacy-law CE in place of all compounding CE.
choice_analysis.C: Supported: Also assess the annual complex-nonsterile compounding CE requirement.
choice_analysis.D: Not supported: Apply compounding CE only to technicians.
choice_analysis.E: Supported: Treat the applicable requirements as cumulative when both activities are supervised.

related_facts: A pharmacist overseeing or directly engaged in covered sterile or complex nonsterile compounding must complete the applicable additional annual compounding continuing-education hours.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'Use general pharmacy-law CE in place of all compounding CE.'

reasoning_steps: Match the scenario's operative facts to Massachusetts compounding continuing education
Reject nearby rules whose schedule, trigger, deadline, or actor differs from Compounding CE
Confirm the exception, documentation, and timing conditions against the cited official authority
